title: Microeconomics and Consumer Theory
text: Microeconomics is the branch of economics that studies individual decision-making — by consumers, firms, and markets — and how these decisions determine prices and the allocation of resources. Consumer theory analyzes how individuals make choices to maximize utility subject to budget constraints, using tools like indifference curves and budget lines. Producer theory analyzes how firms minimize costs and maximize profits given technology and input prices. Market structure — perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition — determines how firms price and compete. Game theory has become a central tool in microeconomics for analyzing strategic interactions between agents.
